newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish parliament approves force for Albania.
newsitem.headline: Danish parliament approves force for Albania.

text.p: Denmark's parliament on Friday approved, by a large cross-party majority, a government proposal to send 65 soldiers to join an Italian-led multinational force in Albania.
The Danish contingent, consisting of staff officers, military police, communications specialists and a reconnaisance unit is expected to join the French battalion in Albania around May 10.

The 6,000-strong main force began arriving on April 15 under a three-month U.N. mandate approved on March 28. So far 2,755 Italian troops, 923 from France, 345 from Spain, 630 from Greece, 691 from Turkey and 116 from Austria are in place.
A further 400 soldiers are due to arrive from Romania on May 4.
The terms of the U.N. mandate for the force allow the troops to secure airports, ports, roads and railways in order to safeguard the distribution of aid.
The resolution says that force can be used in self-defence.

Several hundred people have been killed in Albania since unrest broke out at the end of February, when pyramid investment schemes which sucked in the savings of tens of thousands of Albanians collapsed.

Unofficial estimates say up to a million weapons are in the hands of the country's 3.4 million people, the result of a breakdown of law and order that included raids on police and army depots and barracks.
